site.name: fleetatlas
site.summary: FleetAtlas Fictional commercial fleet real-time management SaaS dashboard, used as a UXBench fixture. Pages - `index.html` — Fleet overview map home. Left thin rail nav; top bar with org switcher, view tabs (Map / List / Analytics), search box, alert bell (dropdown shows the 5 most recent on click); status filter strip (All / Running / Idle / Maintenance / Offline / Alert); full-screen SVG city map with 25 vehicles in real-time positions (running vehicles jitter their position every 5 seconds to simulate live updates); clicking a vehicle icon or drawer row → right detail panel slides in; bottom pull-up drawer showing the vehicle list. - Right detail panel (controlled by JS within the map page) — basic info (plate / model / year / VIN / fleet), driver info (with phone / shift / accumulated drive hours), current task (route / location / ETA / remaining miles), historical track SVG (24h / 7d / 30d toggle), fuel and speed sparklines; 4 action buttons (Send command / Contact driver / Maintenance record / Reassign task), with Reassign being a destructive action that has a second-confirmation modal. - `alerts.html` — Alerts center. 4 KPI cards (open / new today / by severity / mean handli

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full fleetatlas system, prioritizing the primary dashboard flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: FleetAtlas suffers from a critical layout overlap where the left sidebar blocks primary action buttons (Details, Assign) across the app, and severe mobile responsiveness failures causing horizontal overflow and inaccessible controls. Accessibility is also compromised by missing form labels and undersized tap targets. While core filtering and navigation function well on desktop, these overlapping and responsive issues create significant usability blockers for goal completion.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full FleetAtlas system, prioritizing the primary dashboard flow, adjacent pages, interactive states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed through five phases, starting with the primary dashboard map and its dynamic elements, then moving to the vehicle detail panel and its destructive actions. Next, it will validate the alerts center and its filtering capabilities, followed by the analytics and vehicles pages. Finally, it will assess responsive behavior and mobile-specific UX issues across critical flows.
assumptions: The SVG map and vehicle list on the dashboard are interactive and clicking them opens the right detail panel.
The 'Reassign task' button in the detail panel triggers a second-confirmation modal that can be dismissed or confirmed.
The alert bell in the top bar opens a dropdown showing recent alerts without leaving the current page.
Navigation links with '#' (Drivers, Routes, Maintenance, Settings) are placeholder dead-ends and will not load new content.
risk_hotspots: Destructive action: 'Reassign task' button in the right detail panel on index.html
Dynamic content: Vehicle jitter and real-time updates potentially obscuring map interactions or causing layout shifts
Accessibility: Missing label on the org switcher select element across all pages
Mobile usability: Small tap targets on view tabs and left rail navigation items

phases.title: Dashboard Map & Global Controls
phases.objective: Validate the primary dashboard view, map interactions, global controls, and dynamic updates.
key_checks: Switch between Map, List, and Analytics view tabs
Interact with the org switcher dropdown
Click the alert bell to verify the recent alerts dropdown appears
Apply status filters (All, Running, Idle, Maintenance, Offline, Alert) and verify map/list updates
Observe SVG map for vehicle jitter and click a vehicle icon to trigger the detail panel
exit_criteria: All view tabs have been switched
Alert dropdown has been opened and closed
Status filters have been applied and cleared
At least one vehicle icon clicked on the map

phases.title: Vehicle Detail Panel & Actions
phases.objective: Validate the right detail panel, its data display, and action buttons, especially the destructive 'Reassign task' flow.
key_checks: Open detail panel via bottom drawer vehicle list row click
Verify detail panel content: basic info, driver info, current task, historical track toggle (24h/7d/30d)
Click 'Send command', 'Contact driver', and 'Maintenance record' buttons
Click 'Reassign task' and validate the second-confirmation modal appears
Dismiss the confirmation modal without confirming, then close the detail panel
exit_criteria: Detail panel opened via both map icon and list row
Confirmation modal for 'Reassign task' triggered and safely dismissed

phases.title: Alerts Center & Filtering
phases.objective: Validate the alerts page, KPI cards, and multi-faceted filtering capabilities.
key_checks: Navigate to alerts page and verify KPI cards are visible
Interact with time range selector (Last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days)
Apply severity, type, and status filters individually and in combination
Click 'Assign' and 'Details' action buttons on alert rows
Use the alert search input
exit_criteria: Action buttons on at least one alert clicked

phases.title: Analytics & Vehicles Pages
phases.objective: Validate the analytics dashboard data visualizations and the vehicles list page interactions.
key_checks: Navigate to analytics page and verify heatmap and charts render
Review driver performance table
Navigate to vehicles page and use status/fleet filter dropdowns
Use the vehicle search input and interact with checkboxes
Click 'Details' button on a vehicle row
exit_criteria: Vehicles page filters and search exercised

phases.title: Mobile Viewport & Accessibility Checks
phases.objective: Validate critical flows and layout behavior on a mobile viewport, focusing on identified risk hotspots.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and check left rail nav behavior (hamburger menu?)
Validate tap target sizing for view tabs and nav items on index.html
Open vehicle detail panel on mobile and check for overlap or overflow issues
Check alerts page filter layout and usability on small screens
Verify org switcher accessibility on mobile
exit_criteria: Mobile layout assessed on dashboard and alerts pages
Detail panel opens and closes cleanly on mobile
Tap target and layout warnings visually confirmed

coverage_targets.features: exercise all visible filters, search inputs, view tabs, and action buttons; trigger the destructive action modal
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat dashboard map interaction, detail panel opening, and alerts filtering on mobile viewport

notes: Placeholder nav links (Drivers, Routes, Maintenance, Settings) should be clicked to confirm they are dead-ends, but no time spent trying to navigate further.
Pay close attention to the real-time vehicle jitter on the map to ensure it doesn't interfere with clicking vehicles or cause visual bugs.

findings.user_goal: View vehicle or alert details and assign tasks
findings.problem: Primary action buttons like 'Details' and 'Assign' are completely blocked by the left sidebar intercepting pointer events, making it impossible to click them.
findings.evidence: Multiple click attempts on 'Details' (ux-18, ux-68, ux-43, ux-19) and 'Assign' (ux-36) failed with the error: '<aside class="sidebar">…</aside> intercepts pointer events'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users are entirely prevented from completing core tasks like viewing details or assigning alerts, rendering the primary workflows of the application broken.
findings.suggestion: Fix the z-index and layout stacking context of the sidebar so it does not overlap or intercept pointer events on the main content area's action buttons.

findings.user_goal: Use the dashboard and vehicle pages on a mobile device
findings.problem: The layout does not scale down for mobile viewports, causing severe horizontal overflow that forces users to scroll horizontally to access basic controls and data.
findings.evidence: On a 390px mobile viewport, the dashboard page width was 751px, the vehicles page was 916px, and the analytics page was 527px. Bottom navigation items like '⚙️ Settings' were positioned at x=595, far off-screen.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users cannot comfortably view data or navigate the app without constant horizontal scrolling, making the mobile experience highly frustrating and practically unusable.
findings.suggestion: Implement responsive CSS (e.g., flexbox wrapping, fluid grids) to ensure content and navigation fit within the mobile viewport width without horizontal scrolling.

findings.user_goal: Dismiss the alert popover on the dashboard
findings.problem: The alert bell popover cannot be dismissed easily because its close button ('×') is rendered outside the viewport, trapping the user in a blocked state.
findings.evidence: Click attempts on the close button (ux-23, ux-22) failed with the error: 'element is outside of the viewport'. The popover (alertPopover) also blocked clicks on underlying status filter pills.
findings.why_it_matters: Users are stuck with an open popover that obscures other interactive elements, with no visible way to close it, severely disrupting the workflow.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the alert popover is positioned entirely within the viewport bounds and that its close button is visible and accessible at all times.

findings.user_goal: Understand form controls using a screen reader
findings.problem: Critical form controls, including the organization switcher and all filter dropdowns, lack associated labels, aria-labels, or placeholders.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings repeatedly flagged 'missing_input_label' for the org switcher (ux-10, ux-9) and filter dropdowns across all pages (alerts, vehicles, analytics).
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will not know the purpose of these dropdowns, making it impossible to effectively filter data or switch organizations.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit <label> elements or aria-label attributes to all select and input elements (e.g., aria-label='Filter by severity').

findings.user_goal: Tap navigation links, filters, and action buttons on a mobile device
findings.problem: Numerous interactive elements have tap targets smaller than the 44x44px mobile accessibility guideline, making them difficult to activate accurately.
findings.evidence: Status filter pills are 30px high, action buttons like 'Details' are 26px high, checkboxes are 13x13px, and the profile button is 36x36px.
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized tap targets lead to missed taps and user frustration, especially for users with motor impairments or on smaller screens.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and minimum height/width of interactive elements to at least 44x44px to meet mobile touch target guidelines.

findings.user_goal: Search for specific drivers in the analytics table
findings.problem: The search input on the analytics page accepts text but provides no filtering feedback, making it appear broken or non-functional.
findings.evidence: Typing 'James' and pressing Enter into the search input (ux-10) produced no visible filtering or changes to the Driver Performance table.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect search inputs to dynamically filter content; the lack of feedback creates confusion about whether the feature is working.
findings.suggestion: Implement live filtering on the analytics search input, or provide a clear 'No results' message if no matches are found.

findings.user_goal: Understand currently active filters at a glance
findings.problem: When a filter is active, the only indication is the dropdown's selected value; there are no visual tags or highlights reinforcing the active filter state.
findings.evidence: Selecting 'Critical' in the severity filter updated the dropdown and list, but 'there is no additional visual indicator (like a tag or highlight) on the list to reinforce the active filter context'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users might forget that a filter is active, leading to confusion about why certain items are missing from the list.
findings.suggestion: Add visible filter tags or chips above the list when filters are active, providing a clear and easily dismissible indicator of the current view.

findings.user_goal: Access placeholder navigation links like Settings, Drivers, Maintenance, and Routes
findings.problem: Several navigation links in the sidebar are dead-ends (href='#') that provide no visual feedback or navigation when clicked.
findings.evidence: Clicking '🔧 Maintenance' and '👤 Drivers' confirmed they are dead-ends with no navigation or visual response, violating user expectations.
findings.why_it_matters: Dead links erode user trust and make the application feel incomplete or broken.
findings.suggestion: Either implement the destination pages or disable the links and provide a tooltip or visual cue indicating the feature is 'Coming Soon'.

gaps: Only directly exercised 49% of visible interactive feature signatures.
10 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
